chunks: And it is narrated from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, who said:
I said to him: A poor man gives me a gift, seeking what I have; so I take it and do not give him anything. Is it permissible for me?
He said: Yes, it is halal for you, but do not refrain from giving him something.

key_terms.اَلْفَقِيرُ: a poor person in financial need
key_terms.اَلْهَدِيَّةَ: a gift that is offered to another person
key_terms.تُعْطِيَهُ: to give him something in return
key_terms.يَتَعَرَّضُ: seeking indirectly or hoping for what another possesses

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to accept a gift from a poor person without giving anything in return?
ai.summary: This hadith explains that accepting a gift from a poor person is legally permissible even if the giver hopes for something in return. At the same time, it teaches an ethical duty of generosity by encouraging the recipient not to withhold giving something back.
